summary: Texas Forest Service Tower No. 10 in Cherokee County, listed standing; 1946 patrol and 1952 manager records; build date and current access not found.

staffing.status: patrolman in 1946; manager named in 1952; no later staffing reported

events.note: Called Tower No. 10 in a June 1939 newspaper item; construction date not found
Forest Patrolman N.W. Foster reported at the Alto lookout tower in 1946 fire reports
January 1946: Foster reported and suppressed three of nine Cherokee County forest fires; two from careless brush burning, one from a careless smoker
March 1946: Foster handled seven of 34 forest fires recorded in Cherokee County
J.A. Benge, who had managed the Alto tower, moved to Maydelle to take over the fire tower there (January 1952 item)

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build date for the Alto tower. The 'ALTO 1948' on the survey station is a survey marker stamp and is not used as the tower's build year. Staffing facts come from 1946 and 1952 newspaper items as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the 1952 Benge item is the last staffing mention found. 'Standing' comes only from the FFLA Texas list, which is undated. The story says nothing about public access beyond the survey description's gate reference, which is undated, since no source gives current access. The Rusk Cherokeean and Alto Herald originals were not checked; Portal to Texas History may hold the Rusk Cherokeean and could settle the build date. The Alto photo already in the record is not repeated. No new photos added.
